newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Dairy Board calls Kiwi dollar fall "correction".
newsitem.headline: NZ Dairy Board calls Kiwi dollar fall "correction".

text.p: The treasurer of heavyweight New Zealand exporting group The Dairy Board said on Friday he believed the sharp drop in the value of the kiwi dollar against its U.S. counterpart was a timely correction, but that it was unlikely to progress signficantly lower in the medium term.
Dairy Board group treasurer Geoff Taylor told Radio New Zealand news that the kiwi dollar had been too high and had now moved back towards its true value.

"What we're seeing is a correction to an overvalued currency as opposed to a real reversal in fortunes. So we don't believe that the currency will progress significantly lower than this in the near term," he said.

Currency market participants note that many export groups have been busy locking in current levels of the kiwi to help hedge their future overseas earnings during the last few days, anticipating that the kiwi has found a near-term floor.

The Dairy Board, which handles billions of U.S. dollars worth of foreign earnings for its cooperative members, is known to be capable of playing a significant role in the physical and derivative markets.

Taylor made no comment on how the board has acted during the recent movement in the kiwi, which after a steady slide over the last three weeks rattled down one U.S. cent overnight to trade at 0.6507/14 by 2.40 p.m. (0240 GMT) compared with 0.6600 at Thursday's close.

Debt markets have been squeezed by a compensatory rise in short-term rates during this period, as markets seek to maintain the balance of monetary conditions sought by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand in its monetary policy management.
By Friday midsession 90-day bank bill rates had steadied at 8.50 percent, a full 80 basis points higher than Thursday's 7.70 percent close.
